newsitem.title: UK: Britain announces review of surrogacy law.
newsitem.headline: Britain announces review of surrogacy law.

text.p: Britain plans to review laws governing surrogate motherhood following a number of controversial cases, the government announced on Wednesday.

"It is important that in an area as sensitive as surrogacy the law is kept under review in order to ensure that it continues to meet public concerns," Health Minister Tessa Jowell told a parliamentary questioner.

A three-member team will assess whether payment for surrogacy, including expenses, should be allowed, whether changes are needed in the current laws and whether surrogacy arrangements should be regulated through a government body.

"We have specifically asked the review team to consider the issue within the context that surrogacy should not be commercialised and that any woman who has a baby as part of a surrogacy arrangement should not be compelled to give it up if she changes her mind," Jowell added.
The government has been reluctant to change existing laws to curb surrogacy because it already forbids payments, although out-of-pocket expenses are allowed.
The review was called for after several sensational surrogacy cases in Britain.
In January a British woman celebrated the birth of a baby boy that was born 22 months after his twin sister in a surrogacy arrangement which gave the children three mothers.
The twins were conceived in a test tube from the same batch of eggs but carried to term by two different surrogate mothers.

Another British woman, who was acting as a surrogate mother for a childless Dutch couple, lied to them that she had aborted their baby. It later emerged that she had struck a deal to give the unborn baby to another couple.
The British Medical Association, which represents doctors, has said surrogate pregnancies are acceptable as a last resort for infertile couples when other fertility treatments have failed.
But it said surrogacy contracts could not be enforced in law, and that such arrangements were fraught with problems.
